blockers.quote: > HOLD: 4 s. A paper snap above your own head, out of frame. His grin stops, on your face, not the air above it. You look up, and can't see your own card. We never see the number.
blockers.why: No new power rule after the halfway point: the film has never established that another person's news opens a card over you or that your own card is invisible to you.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "> HOLD: 4 s. He says it and grins. Your eyes lift to the empty air over your own head. Nothing opens. You look back at him. Cut before your answer."

blockers.quote: Your score reaches the top. The desk beside you is empty.
blockers.why: Check #11, Never say the feeling: this only captions the rank list and empty desk already shown.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "You got the place you wanted. And lost the one beside it."

blockers.quote: Then the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. He says it.
blockers.why: Check #12, Leave fast: the final story image has staging and a CTA, but no line that turns the opening or gives the image meaning.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Then the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. He says it. For the first time, the good news isn't yours."

suggestions.quote: So you climb the academy steps and say it into the crowd.
suggestions.fix: Replace with: "So you climb the academy steps, find your best friend's face in the crowd, and say it loud enough for the street." This closes the face-to-face loophole.

suggestions.quote: We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below (c10).
suggestions.fix: Merge lines 97–99 into: "We compare ourselves with people near our level, especially when they started where we did and the thing matters (c10, c12)."

suggestions.quote: Couples where one partner meets good news with enthusiasm report more intimacy and satisfaction (c09).
suggestions.fix: Cut this line; the relationship studied is not the sibling relationship shown, and line 244 already drives the departure.

keep.quote: Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.
A card has one colour for every kind of hurt.
A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
